sections.title: Ultra-Low Latency Data Fabric
sections.body: Large-scale AI training is not just about the speed of individual GPUs; it is about the speed at which those GPUs can talk to each other. Kenya AI Compute has implemented a non-blocking Spine-Leaf network topology that provides predictable, low-latency communication between any two ports in our facility. Our core is 400G-ready, with 100G uplinks standard for every compute node. We utilize RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE v2) to allow GPUs to share memory directly across the network, bypassing the CPU bottleneck. Externally, we maintain diverse fiber routes to the international cable landing stations in Mombasa. This multi-carrier strategy ensures that your AI APIs and DePIN nodes stay connected to the global internet with the lowest possible hop count to major IXPs in Europe and the Middle East. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models. sections.title: Network Specifications
items: Topology: Spine-Leaf architecture for massive horizontal scalability.
Throughput: 100 Gbps per server node with 400G core uplinks.
Interconnect: Full support for RDMA/RoCE v2 and InfiniBand options.
External: 3+ independent fiber entry points for carrier neutrality.
Security: Hardware-level DDoS mitigation and VLAN isolation.
